neighbours.label: the content of a fronted temporal 'when' clause (its verb or object, up to the comma), before the main clause arrives
fire: When cleaning a cast iron pan, avoid soap.
When I uploaded the photos to my page, a friend noticed the mistake.
When painting a ceiling, cover the floor first.
Back when the railway was first being laid, the town had two shops.
When choosing a puppy, watch how it plays with others.
When she opened the letter, her hands were shaking.
When storing fresh herbs, wrap them in a damp towel.
When the first phones arrived, few homes could afford one.
quiet: Cast iron pans should not be washed with soap.
I uploaded the photos to my page, and a friend noticed the mistake.
Cover the floor first and then paint the ceiling.
The railway was first laid in the town in 1870.
Watch how a puppy plays with others before you choose one.
She opened the letter with shaking hands.
Fresh herbs keep longer in a damp towel.
The first phones were too expensive for most homes.
